parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a protective state with a hostile federal layer that governs every journey stage a visitor actually passes: border screening, airports, federal buildings, and immigration custody. Universal exposures dominate — the March/November 2025 passport-marker regime with documented strandings and cable instructions to refuse cases casting doubt on sex, federal exclusion from government-funded single-sex facilities (airports included), and documented abuse in immigration custody. State law offsets daily life: public-accommodations and healthcare nondiscrimination, hate-crime enhancements, panic-defense repeal, no documented state facility ban or violence record. Courts function but have upheld the passport rule. The visitor's exposure follows the federal layer, not the state's top-tier ranking.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 X-marker/marker-mismatch processing ban; Nov 2025 Supreme Court let restrictions take effect; trans travellers report passports confiscated or blocked, stranded abroad; Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse cases where records cast reasonable doubt on sex and to consider lifetime fraud ineligibility. At least eight foreign governments issued travel advisories by April 2025.
entry_documents.protection: The civil-liberties union suit on behalf of seven plaintiffs remains pending in national courts; a legal-aid organisation runs a running FAQ on passport/document rules. No documented operative protection at the border itself.
entry_documents.interaction: A visitor's home passport is checked at federal entry desks inside this jurisdiction; state document-friendliness (self-declaration licences, X marker) does not touch federal adjudication of foreign documents.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: In immigration custody, transgender men reportedly subjected to forced-labour programmes, beatings, solitary confinement for refusal, and severe sexual abuse; national corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style inmate policies from 2026 (hair cutting, hormone removal) and stopped reporting transgender prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several executive orders blocked or enjoined; federal courts functioning; state listed 'Most Protective' with hate-crime and nondiscrimination machinery. No documented visitor-specific custody protocol.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy at entry can escalate into federal investigation and custody, where birth-sex placement and the documented custody abuses become operative — state protections do not reach federal detention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity — covering federal buildings and airports nationwide, a continuous universal exposure at every federal site the visitor enters. Parent map shows bans in 21+ state/provinces, criminal trespass triggers in 4, and a documented 2025 arrest elsewhere.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province has no documented facility ban; nondiscrimination in public accommodations since 2001; single-occupancy gender-neutral toilets since 2022.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Daily venues in the state are protected, but the visitor's airport, federal courthouses and national buildings follow the federal order regardless of state law.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders frame gender-affirming care as mutilation, freeze funding, propose barring insurance reimbursement for under-18s, and subpoenaed 'over 20' hospitals for under-19 patient records; care access for travelling minors sits inside this federal hostility.
care_services.protection: State statutes bar discrimination in patient care, nursing and related healthcare (June 2023 additions); state appears on the shield-law/executive-order map (2023–2024 batches) enforceable against out-of-state action.
care_services.interaction: Shield-law scope for visitors seeking care is explicitly unresolved; federal funding and record-subpoena powers operate inside the state regardless.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; Dec 2025 reward memorandum invokes 'radical gender ideology'; Jan 2025 order directs law enforcement against teachers facilitating social transition; 2025 poll: 66% back sex-at-birth document rules; advocates compare the administration's trajectory to early genocide stages.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute; 2020 employment ruling; state hate-crime penalty enhancements (§ 42-28-46) and gay/trans panic defence repealed 2018.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing raises outing and enforcement probability at borders and federal sites; state law mitigates street and venue encounters within the state.

minors_guardians.exposure: Jan 2025 order criminalising facilitation of a trans minor's social transition; Jan 2025 order calling minors' care 'mutilation'; care banned in 27 state/provinces; hospital-record subpoenas; facility bans reach K-12 in 21+ units. A trans parent or trans minor travelling here meets this federal framing.
minors_guardians.protection: State conversion-therapy ban since 2017, anti-bullying statute covering gender identity, shield laws, nondiscrimination in patient care; state not documented among the 27 care-ban units.
minors_guardians.interaction: A care-seeking or school-adjacent stop inside the state can trigger federal investigative and funding machinery the state cannot switch off.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-level anti-trans violence incident or dated prevalence figure exists in the inventory; national bias statistics track sexual orientation, not gender identity; social climate signal: 66% public support for sex-at-birth document rules.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime enhancements for gender-identity-motivated offences, panic defence unavailable since 2018, public-accommodations protection since 2001, national hate-crime statute.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street encounters occur under state law with working enforcement machinery, but officer discretion at federal sites follows federal policy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport restrictions upheld by the Supreme Court; state statutes have no documented enforcement data (no complaint volumes or outcomes); shield-law scope for visitors unresolved; state-credential interaction with federal entry rules unsourced; several orders remain merely enjoined, so exposure shifts with litigation timing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Pending ACLU suit, legal-aid FAQ, federal courts blocking multiple orders, state ranked 'Most Protective' with operative nondiscrimination, hate-crime and panic-defense-repeal statutes.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are real but federal and slow; they do not reverse an entry refusal or a custody placement in the moment.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-A: Vellandra's Visitor Conduct Register excludes trans visitors with near-zero remedy and no domestic protection at all. Here the state layer supplies public-accommodations, healthcare and hate-crime protection with functioning courts, and the entry regime, though hostile, retains waiver avenues and active litigation rather than an unpublished exclusion register.

Closest match. Vesskar shows routine checkpoint exposure, lengthy verification, documented detention, humiliation and denial of care with slow, unreliable remedies. The dossier's federal document/entry regime mirrors this, and adds documented custody abuse and a federal facility ban — offset by stronger operative state protections than Vesskar's narrow anti-discrimination claim.

Lower than 0.55-B: Kestrel Isles' secondary screening ends in administrative refusal with written decisions, appeal desks and consular notification, no custody abuse. Here screening can escalate to documented immigration-custody violence, federal facility exclusion is universal, and the passport regime is backed by statute and Supreme Court blessing rather than discretion alone.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system is layered: the state's 2001-era nondiscrimination, hate-crime enhancements, panic-defense repeal and shield laws protect daily life — hotels, restaurants, state buildings, clinics — while the federal layer controls every stage the visitor cannot avoid: entry adjudication, airports, federal facilities, and immigration custody. Those federal exposures are universal and documented (marker regime with strandings, refusal-on-doubt cable, facility exclusion, custody abuse), and several have survived judicial review. The state's ranking is therefore real but partial; the July 2026 map itself says the top tier can no longer be considered most protective nationwide. Combined, this sits mid-scale: no criminalisation of identity, working courts and strong local protections, but continuous federal exposure with severe low-probability custody outcomes and no effective real-time remedy.
